# Step: 13-step-npm-package-test

## Ownership

- Goal: `16-toolchain-and-packaging`
- Work unit: `W120`
- Type: `test`

## Change target

- File: `planning/tests/test-npm-package.sh`
- Primary symbol or file scope: `npm_package_install_flow`
- Subscope: `N/A`

## Objective

§ 4.1
Pack and extract the npm tarball in a clean temporary directory and compare it with the single W105-owned planning/tests/fixtures/overview/npm-package-baseline.tsv record. Invoke the generated installer through W104 test-only platform inputs and assert the supported and unsupported results without defining a second package file list or byte-size baseline.

## Instructions

§ 5.1
Create tmp with mktemp and install a trap that removes tmp and the captured tarball and returns non-zero on cleanup failure. Set tarball to the output of npm pack --silent without evaluating it during test construction. Extract with tar -xzf tarball into tmp and set pkg to tmp/package. Read planning/tests/fixtures/overview/npm-package-baseline.tsv as the only expected package record. Assert its fixed header, sorted package_path rows, exact tarball file list and final tarball_bytes value against the freshly packed tarball. Invoke the extracted installer from pkg with PLAN_OVERVIEW_TEST_MODE=1 PLAN_OVERVIEW_TEST_OS=Linux PLAN_OVERVIEW_TEST_ARCH=x86_64 and install-root tmp/install-linux. Repeat with macOS arm64 inputs and Windows_NT AMD64 inputs through the same installer path. For unsupported Windows use PLAN_OVERVIEW_TEST_MODE=1 PLAN_OVERVIEW_TEST_OS=Windows_NT PLAN_OVERVIEW_TEST_ARCH=ARM64 and assert no artifact. Assert exactly one selected executable per supported install plus successful render and serve readiness and state responses. Assert no artifact and the exact unavailable notice for unsupported input. Remove tmp and tarball on exit and make cleanup failure non-zero.

## Acceptance criteria

§ 6.1
The repository test exits zero only when the clean extracted tarball sorted file list exactly matches the W105-owned baseline record and its byte size equals the final tarball_bytes value; each supported test-only platform input selects exactly one runnable artifact and produces successful render and serve output; the unsupported Windows architecture places none and emits the exact unavailable notice; and cleanup succeeds. A missing or stale baseline fails rather than being regenerated by W120.

## Handoff

§ 7.1
W106 repeats the lifecycle on real platform hosts; W48 runs this shell test after W113 has regenerated install.sh. W105 remains the only owner that generates or refreshes the package baseline.
